payload.title: Wedding Morning Timeline for the Getting Ready Hours
secondary_keywords: what time should hair and makeup start on wedding day
bridal party hair and makeup schedule
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their 30s with a ceremony time set (often at a destination venue, with a suite or villa as the getting-ready base) who now needs to know when hair and makeup should start, in what order each person goes, and when the photographer should arrive, so they can brief their stylist, artist and photographer with one agreed morning.
payload.goal: Start a conversation with a Wedded Advisor through the Wedded Concierge enquiry form to have the wedding morning planned around the venue and the ceremony time.
secondary_links: /expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline (head page; link prominently near the top as the full-day guide; it should link here from its getting-ready section)
/expert-advice/wedding-timeline-4pm-ceremony (sibling; link from the sample morning) [[VERIFY: link-map status is draft as at 2026-11-24; link only once live, otherwise LINK comment]]
/expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline-template (full-day template; link from the template section)
/expert-advice/bridal-hair-trial-and-makeup-trial--should-you-have-one- (the trial is where timing per person is confirmed)
/style/how-to-make-wedding-makeup-last-in-humid-weather (from the destination heat and humidity section)
WW-127 beauty prep countdown: planned, not live. LINK comment only, never a live link.
payload.angle: The getting-ready hours in close-up: a morning worked backwards from the ceremony (when you need to be dressed, when getting-ready photos happen, the order each person sits for hair and makeup), with a sample morning for a 4pm ceremony that matches our 4pm timeline exactly (hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or 10am without, photographer at 12.30pm or 1.30pm, guests arriving at 3.30pm) and how it slides for earlier and later starts. It answers the hair and makeup timing questions honestly: every clock time is an example, and how long each person takes is a question for your stylist and artist, never a stated figure. Framed for destination mornings, where heat, humidity, the suite or villa as base and the distance to the ceremony site are questions for the venue.
must_include: Direct-answer intro (how a wedding morning is built, in a sentence or two), followed by exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways.

Working backwards from the ceremony: when to be dressed and ready, when getting-ready photos fit, and the order of hair and makeup per person (who goes first and last, and why the couple usually finishes last). No durations stated as fact; tell readers to ask their stylist and artist.

A sample morning for a 4pm ceremony consistent with /expert-advice/wedding-timeline-4pm-ceremony: hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or 10am without; photographer at 12.30pm with a first look or 1.30pm without; guests arriving at 3.30pm. Then how the morning moves for earlier and later starts (keep to the 4pm page's example starts: 7.30am for 2pm, 8.30am for 3pm, 11am for 5pm). All times framed 'for example'.
How many people are getting ready shapes the start time: more people means an earlier start or a second stylist or artist; ask your stylist and artist to work back from your ready time.
The getting-ready space: natural light, room for the photographer to work, food and water, and one person keeping time.

Destination mornings as questions to ask the venue: heat and humidity (link the humid-weather makeup piece), the suite or villa as base (access time, room for everyone), and the distance and travel time to the ceremony site.
A copyable morning schedule template (table with blank times the reader fills in, working back from the ceremony).
FAQ section (e.g. what time should hair and makeup start, who goes first, when should the photographer arrive, how much buffer to leave).

Close with one Wedded Advisor line drawn only from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' (e.g. one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, working in your time zone), linking /wonderland-concierge with UTM.
Prominent link to /expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline near the top.
avoid: Stating how long hair or makeup takes per person, or any duration as fact; refer to the stylist and artist.
Any example time that contradicts the 4pm page (9am/10am start, 12.30pm/1.30pm photographer, 3.30pm guests; 7.30am, 8.30am, 11am for 2pm, 3pm, 5pm).
The phrase 'last dance' anywhere (brand-facts' Advisor definition uses it); use 'the send-off' if needed.
Prices of any kind, 'From AUD' figures, statistics, 'best', 'free', vendor names.
Research or process talk ('our research shows', 'top results', 'SERP').
Advisor claims outside 'Claims we can make': no 'on the ground', transfers, room blocks, phone line or a named person.
Skincare, beauty prep weeks out, or trial content in depth; summarise and link (trial page; WW-127 as LINK comment).
Re-covering the full day after the ceremony; link the head and 4pm pages.
Competitor names, wording or formats; clichés; em dashes; US spelling.
